purpose: Problem-family assimilation routines for M2D-SBA-21 after concept teaching and before Revised Core (2) transfer.

transfer_routines.title: Range on an inclined plane
recognition_signals: projectile lands on a sloping line through the launch point
impact point or distance along the incline is asked

method_steps.title: Put both objects in the same axes
method_steps.learner_move: Write the projectile trajectory and plane equation y=x tan(beta).

method_steps.title: Translate impact into an intersection
method_steps.learner_move: Set y_projectile=y_plane at the same x.

method_steps.title: Keep the landing root
method_steps.learner_move: Factor out x and reject x=0 when looking for the later impact.

method_steps.title: Convert horizontal projection to inclined distance

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile is launched at 15 m/s at 60 degrees above the horizontal and lands on a 30 degree incline through the launch point. Take g=10 m/s^2. Find the distance along the incline to impact.
independent_practice.answer_check: The non-zero intersection gives x=15sqrt(3)/2 m; s=x/cos30 degrees=15 m.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Impact is the second intersection of the projectile path and the inclined line; do not set y=0.

hint_ladder.label: Representation
hint_ladder.prompt: Write y=x tan30 degrees and y=x tan60 degrees-gx^2/(2u^2 cos^2 60 degrees).

hint_ladder.label: First move
hint_ladder.prompt: Set those two y-values equal and keep the non-zero root.

readiness_checks: recognise that the landing condition is an intersection
write plane and projectile in the same ground axes
reject the launch root x=0 without a hint
convert horizontal x to along-plane s correctly
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q54 after 4/4 readiness without H2/H3.

transfer_routines.title: Inclined-plane projection geometry
recognition_signals: time t is already known or directly usable
horizontal component gives the projection AC
the requested length lies along the incline

method_steps.title: Draw the right triangle
method_steps.learner_move: Mark x as the horizontal projection of the along-plane distance s.

method_steps.title: Solve the requested length
method_steps.learner_move: Use s=x/cos(beta) and check s exceeds x for a rising incline.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile has speed 24 m/s at 60 degrees. After 2.0 s it is at a point on a 30 degree incline through the launch point. Find its distance along the incline from the launch point.
independent_practice.answer_check: x=24 cos60 degrees times 2=24 m; s=24/cos30 degrees=16sqrt(3) m, about 27.7 m.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Use the stated time to find the horizontal projection first.

hint_ladder.label: Representation
hint_ladder.prompt: Write x=(24 cos60 degrees)(2), then draw x=s cos30 degrees.

readiness_checks: find x from the horizontal component and time
draw x=s cos beta without a hint
check that along-plane distance is longer than its horizontal projection

transfer_routines.title: Normal impact on an incline
recognition_signals: projectile must hit the incline normally
the launch angle must be designed to satisfy point and direction conditions together

method_steps.title: Translate normal into a direction
method_steps.learner_move: For plane angle beta, impact velocity points at beta+90 degrees from +x.

method_steps.title: Write the velocity condition
method_steps.learner_move: Use v_x=u cos(alpha), v_y=u sin(alpha)-gt and v_y/v_x=-cot(beta).

method_steps.title: Write the point-on-plane condition
method_steps.learner_move: At the same time t, impose y=x tan(beta).

method_steps.title: Eliminate the shared impact time
method_steps.learner_move: Combine both constraints, then solve for alpha and check alpha>beta.

independent_practice.prompt: A projectile must hit an incline normally. The incline satisfies tan(beta)=1/2. For the ideal model, find the required launch angle alpha above the horizontal.
independent_practice.answer_check: Combining the point and velocity constraints gives tan(alpha-beta)=1/(2tan beta)=1. Hence alpha=beta+45 degrees, about 71.6 degrees.

hint_ladder.label: Key physics
hint_ladder.prompt: Normal impact means the velocity is perpendicular to the incline, not vertical.

hint_ladder.label: Representation
hint_ladder.prompt: Use v_y/v_x=-cot(beta) together with the point condition y=x tan(beta).

hint_ladder.label: First move
hint_ladder.prompt: Write v_x=u cos(alpha) and v_y=u sin(alpha)-gt, then impose the velocity ratio before eliminating t.

readiness_checks: recognise normal impact as a direction condition
write the component ratio for the normal direction
write the point-on-plane condition at the same time
combine both constraints to solve a fresh launch-angle problem
transfer_routines.release_rule: Release Q56 after 4/4 readiness without H2/H3.
